notes:
Account background: Peakwise builds an in-product analytics assistant for B2B product teams (search + contextual chat + release-note summarization). Currently using OpenAI + custom reranker; looking to move to Redwood Hosted for cost + control, then Dedicated for production isolation.

Key asks from product: 
- Prompt parity: identical outputs for ~80% of top-50 prompts; deterministic behaviour on system messages and function/tool calling.
- Latency SLOs: 95th pct < 400ms for chat flow under burst of 50 qps.
- Throughput: batch reranks of up to 512 embeddings per second; embed indexer needs steady throughput for nightly jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: current vendor spend ~$18k/mo; target 30-45% unit-cost reduction on tokens/embeds.
- Security: SOC2, SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and EU data residency for small subset of customers.

Migration concerns flagged on kickoff call: 
- "We can't afford regressions in release note summaries" — PM emphasized human QA on top 100 prompts.
- Tokenization differences cause small diffs in completions; devs worried about downstream tests failing.
- Function calling parity (name/param ordering) — existing infra depends on stable signatures.

Demo & POC plan: 
- 2026-01-14: initial Hosted API demo (Jordan, Priya, Lead PM, Eng mgr). Positive: streaming + function calls demoed, model catalog looked good. Action: provide a compatibility checklist and sample client lib.
- 2026-01-22: follow-up tech deep-dive; provided sandbox keys and prompt-parity checklist. Eng asked for token-level cost reports.
- 2026-02-05: Redwood ran side-by-side perf profile vs current vendor on 25 representative prompts — 3/25 prompts showed measurable style/regression differences (brevity/temperature).
- 2026-02-18: pricing review call; SE delivered Dedicated node sizing estimate and rough TCO for 12-month commit.

POC scope agreed: 2-week seeded traffic test on Redwood Hosted with production traffic mirroring (A/B 1:1), run regression suite (top-100 prompts) and collect token-level cost/latency metrics. If parity < threshold or regressions > 5%, iterate on model variant/config (quant, temp, decode params).

Open action items: 
- Redwood: provide compatibility shim guidance + example request/response diff tool (PRI).
- Peakwise Eng: build integration harness to replay traffic and wire audit logs to S3 (ETA 2/16).
- Legal: exchange security appendix (Peakwise legal requests data residency clause for EU customers).

Stated quotes from stakeholders: 
- Lead PM: "We want the same answers or better — can't ship worse summaries to customers."
- Head of Infra: "If you can show 35% savings at parity we'll move to Dedicated."

Notes on technical regressions discovered: 
- Small differences in spacing/punctuation due to tokenizer merging — causes failing QA snapshots for release-note templates. Redwood suggested tokenization mapping and post-processing normalization as interim.
- Reranker scores slightly reordered for 8% of queries; SE recommended tuning temperature/beam and trying a retrain on top-of-index embeddings.

Risk profile: medium — good product fit and clear incentive to switch (cost + observability), but migration risk centers on regressions and legal/SLA timeline.

Last meeting: 2026-02-28 POC kickoff. Redwood delivered sandbox hosted keys and POC checklist. Peakwise requested Dedicated pricing with 12-month and 24-month options by 2026-03-07.
